analysis: Both changed files are documentation only: docs/developer/test.md (head lines 2465-2485, new section 'Cluster service listeners after pairing again') and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (head lines 581-588, new troubleshooting bullet). No executable code, keys, endpoints, attestation logic or coordinator-provider contract is changed in the supplied evidence. The docs describe a behavior change in the cluster service: listeners refuse the earlier pairing with handshakeRejected after re-pairing, restart with the new pairing, stop on a removed pairing, keep the same listeners on an unchanged or unreadable store, and drop the old control node. If accurate, this strengthens revocation of the old pairing. The troubleshooting note says a service started by an earlier release keeps the earlier pairing, so it continues to accept the stale pairing until restarted (`darkbloom cluster stop`, then `darkbloom cluster`). That is a documented operational and transition caveat, not a regression introduced by these docs. Cluster pairing and the two-Mac listeners are not a defined trust boundary in the supplied threat model; the relevant IDs (TB-002, TB-003, TB-011, T-041 etc.) are not directly affected. The provider-swift sources the docs cite (ClusterService.Listening, the pairing store reading, the tests) were not supplied, so the documented claims, including fail-safe handling of an unreadable pairing store, are unverified. The code change that implements them should be reviewed in its own pass for stale-pairing acceptance, the downgrade window with old-release services, and whether an unreadable store keeps old listeners alive. No findings from these docs alone.
